Q1: The `resolve` path, its kill switch and the poll-job step that calls it exist only in open PR #9259, not on main. Which code should this follow-up audit and fix?
Choices:
A) Wait until #9259 merges, then audit and fix the merged code on main, adding only the missing contract tests and fixes. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Branch from #9259's head and add the tests and fixes on top of it, so this PR depends on #9259 merging first.
C) If #9259 has not merged, build the `resolve` path from scratch on main as plan P10 describes. **Note:** this duplicates #9259 and will conflict with it.
Q2: When should `resolve` treat an entry's consumer-sync condition as met?
Choices:
A) The same way as a release condition: the entry's merge commit is contained in `stable` (`compare/<merge_sha>...stable` returns `ahead` or `identical`). Consumer sync runs automatically from the `@stable` release (plan P10.1). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Contained in `stable`, and also each repo in `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` shows it has synced. This adds calls for each consumer repo per tick, beyond plan P10's limit of 10 compare calls per tick.
C) Never tick consumer-sync entries automatically; only tick release entries.
